summary.headline: Max Healthcare Q4 FY26 revenue rose 10% YoY to INR 2,664 crore, but EBITDA margin slipped to 26.8% on chemo-drug discontinuation and higher ALOS.
summary.overview: Network gross revenue grew 10% YoY and 2% QoQ to INR 2,664 crore, and operating EBITDA rose 8% YoY to INR 682 crore, marking the 22nd consecutive quarter of YoY growth. Margin fell to 26.8% from 27.2% a year ago, as higher ALOS (up 9% YoY) and the discontinuation of select high-value chemotherapy drugs for institutional patients weighed on ARPOB (INR 77,900) and oncology share. For FY26, revenue grew 16% to INR 10,538 crore, EBITDA rose 14% to INR 2,638 crore and PAT rose 22% to INR 1,631 crore. Management also completed control of Kalinga Hospital (250 beds, Bhubaneswar) and approved a INR 1,400 crore, 700-bed greenfield in Lucknow.

guidance_outlook: Kalinga Hospital (250 beds, Bhubaneswar) consolidated from Q1 FY27; already at about INR 10 crore annual EBITDA, with plans to revamp and expand the site.

Gurugram Sector 56 (500 beds) commissioning targeted by end of FY27, after slipping from earlier second-half guidance; expected to start with about 200 beds and break even in FY28 (Dwarka precedent: broke even in 6 months).
Chemo-drug discontinuation: annual chemotherapy billing down about INR 200 crore; oncology share expected to hover at 21-22%, not return to 25-26%.
CGHS rate revision: about INR 100-110 crore annualised already flowing; balance INR 30-40 crore (super-specialty rates) expected over coming months.
Brownfield capacity: about 20% added (Mohali, Nanavati, Max Smart) with balance beds to open over next 2-3 months; Lucknow Gomti Nagar to rise to 570 beds over next 2 quarters.
Lucknow Shaheed Path: 700-bed greenfield (INR 1,400 crore), phased over about 3 years, expandable to about 900 beds.
risks_watch: Oncology volume loss (OBDs down 5-6%) and patients possibly shifting to unorganised sectors or smaller nursing homes; ECHS and PSU patients may face access issues to drugs such as Keytruda.
Uncertain timing for CGHS reconsidering the chemo discount; any reversal is not time-bound.
Gurugram 500-bed greenfield has slipped several times; commissioning by end of FY27 and early breakeven are key checkpoints.
Doctor compensation pressure as multiple micro-markets add capacity; Q4 doctor costs of about INR 435 crore.
ALOS normalisation and ARPOB recovery as brownfield beds ramp; margin of 26.8% vs 27.2% a year ago.
Kalinga integration and the revamp plan; the company did not disclose the acquisition consideration in this call.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the expansion pipeline, demand and new-hospital ramp-ups (Dwarka, Noida, Lucknow), but cautious and somewhat defensive on the chemo-drug discontinuation, which management said is largely permanent. Timelines for CGHS reversal and Gurugram were hedged with reasons for slippage.
key_quotes: Average occupancy for the Network continued to be more than 75% despite increase in operational bed capacity, with most of the units operating at near optimal capacity.
We do not expect the share of oncology come back to 25-26% as it was earlier. It will continue to hover around 21-22%.
None of these acquisitions have been loss-making or even after taking over when we did whatever actions we took, it did not go into a negative territory.

qa_highlights.question: When will the brownfield beds contribute to EBITDA more meaningfully, and will occupancy ramp well?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said brownfield beds already contribute positively. Operating leverage will come as the balance beds open over the next couple of quarters, since costs are not linear. Occupancy stays high, but higher ALOS (+9% YoY) is temporary and lowers ARPOB.

qa_highlights.question: Will Gurugram be commissioned by end of this fiscal year and how many beds will open in FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Commissioning is expected by end of FY27. Gurugram starts with about 200 beds and is expected to break even within FY28. Dwarka broke even in 6 months against 1-year guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Why did oncology share drop sharply in Q4, and will it reverse?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the discontinuation of high-value chemo drugs affected day-care margins (about 16%, now below a 30%-of-MRP CGHS discount) and reduced oncology OBDs by about 5-6%. Some of the loss is permanent, with oncology share expected at 21-22%. CGHS reconsideration timing is uncertain.

qa_highlights.question: What is the chemo discontinuation impact on revenue and EBITDA, and is it annual or quarterly?
qa_highlights.answer: Annual chemotherapy billing is down about INR 200 crore gross (about INR 140 crore net of GST). Q4 has the full impact, with discontinuation starting October 2025. CGHS rate revision adds INR 100-110 crore annualised so far, with INR 30-40 crore still to come.

qa_highlights.question: Which hospitals have doctor cost pressure, and will Q4 doctor costs (about INR 435 crore) stay at this level?
qa_highlights.answer: Doctor hiring followed the 25-30% capacity addition in late 2024 and the current 20%+ brownfield rollout across Mohali, Nanavati, Smart and Lucknow. Management expects doctor cost ratios to decline with operating leverage. Kalinga will add manpower but will not move the needle.

qa_highlights.question: How do the Lucknow land bank and the Shaheed Path greenfield fit together, and is there cannibalisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Gomti Nagar (27 acres) will reach 570 beds, with another 200-300 beds planned there. Shaheed Path (5+ acres) is a 700-bed phased project over about 3 years, expandable to about 900 beds. It is a multi-location cluster strategy rather than cannibalisation.

capex_capacity: Brownfield: over the last two quarters, phased commissioning of more than 20% additional brownfield capacity at Mohali, Nanavati (Mumbai) and Max Smart (Delhi); remaining beds to be operationalised over the next 2-3 months. Management also expects another ~10% capacity from the 500-bed Gurugram greenfield on commissioning.

Gurugram Sector 56 (500 beds): interior and facade works started; commissioning targeted by end of FY27 after slipping from earlier 'middle of second half' guidance, due to labour attrition during state elections, LPG shortage affecting contractor labour (company now serving meals to ~1,100-1,200 workers) and about a couple of months of delay. Initial operations expected at ~200 beds; breakeven targeted within FY28 (Dwarka precedent: 300 beds, started with 140, breakeven in 6 months vs 12-month guidance, H1 EBITDA loss ~INR 35 crore).

Max Lucknow Gomti Nagar: 426 beds currently, rising to 570 beds over the next 2 quarters; further 200-300 beds planned on the 27-acre Gomti Nagar land bank over time. Lucknow Shaheed Path: 700-bed greenfield approved at INR 1,400 crore, phased over ~3 years, expandable to ~900 beds; 5+ acres.

Pipeline (commissioning in next 2-3 years): Max Nagpur 100 beds by FY28; Zirakpur, Mohali 400 beds in FY28; Max Dwarka 260 beds (building plan submission underway, 24 months); Max Vaishali 200 beds (awaiting building plan approvals, 24 months post approval); Max Patparganj 400 beds with D-wall construction started, commissioning by FY29. Dwarka brownfield of 200-plus beds being planned; Dwarka oncology centre to start next month.

Kalinga Hospital (Bhubaneswar, 250 beds, 10-acre site): controlling stake acquired in May 2026, consolidation from Q1 FY27; about INR 10 crore annual EBITDA; plans to revamp and expand. Acquisition consideration not discussed.

FY26 capital deployment: INR 1,627 crore into ongoing expansion projects and facility upgrades at newer units, INR 131 crore for land at Vaishali, INR 146 crore dividend paid; Q4 deployment INR 328 crore.
demand_pricing: Network Q4 occupancy above 75% despite higher operational beds; OBDs up 8% YoY and 4% QoQ; ALOS up 9% YoY due to simultaneous multi-location brownfield rollout, expected to tighten over time.

ARPOB INR 77,900 in Q4, after absorbing higher ALOS and discontinuation of select high-value chemotherapy drugs for institutional patients (CGHS). Oncology OBDs down ~5-6% YoY; oncology share of in-patient revenue 21% vs 26% in Q4 FY25 and 24% in Q3 FY26. Management expects oncology share to hover at 21-22%, not return to 25-26%.

Chemo-drug discontinuation: discontinued since October 2025; annual chemotherapy billing down ~INR 200 crore (gross); net of GST ~INR 140 crore. Earlier drugs were billed at MRP with ~15-16% margins; CGHS now requires ~30% discount to MRP. Management says this is industry-wide but Max is most affected given oncology and institutional mix. Q4 carries the full impact.

CGHS rate revision: ~INR 100-110 crore annualised already flowing; balance INR 30-40 crore (super-specialty rates, at two hospitals so far) to flow over the coming months. Management said CGHS is reconsidering the chemo discount but timing is not fixed. ECHS and PSU patients lack dispensary access to drugs such as Keytruda.

Noida ramp-up: occupancy above 64-65% in Q4 with doctors hired; management says it is in line with expectations. Dwarka at 80-85% occupancy. Management cited a hockey-stick occupancy curve: units break even around 50-55% occupancy, and the real value comes from 60-65% to about 80%.

Other metrics: Max@Home revenue INR 73 crore (+30% YoY, 16 service lines, 15 cities); Max Lab revenue INR 52 crore (+14% YoY, 60+ cities, ~6 lakh patients); international patient revenue INR 227 crore (+12% YoY, 9% of hospital revenue); digital revenue INR 838 crore (~31% of revenue). Q4 doctor costs about INR 435 crore; management expects operating leverage from here.
Management stated the company sees 10-12% PAT margin as the industry's steady state. It said doctor compensation increases in micro-markets are transferred to patients over time.
